verifications.note: Independently judged by release-auditor (T-DG5-RG2-AUDIT-V, session 69bfb4f2) on candidate sha256:55a411ae9f4e87473478988f3d9909752a934a547ba40acc1479f2b2bc3a24ce (source 660f40c7d141b6fb73c145e0ee7a053ceb5905de), in my own complete clone. I confirmed the defect: migration 0062 seeds the five scoring_weight elements with sourceLabelEn and labelAr but no labelEn, and apps/web/src/pages/studio/api.ts elementLabel() (lines 138-146) reads only labelEn/labelAr, so the English Studio Elements table falls back to Arabic. I also saw it in domain's round-2 screenshot screens/en/dom-p3-published.png. Reach: elementLabel has exactly one caller (studio/ElementsSection.tsx:372, the methodology administrator's Elements table). None of the 13 server files that consume scoring_weight (publish, scoring-defaults, invariants, rankings, scores, gate-facts, prioritization, the demo seed) reads a label attribute; only the shared zod schema validates them. The scoring-defaults editor names criteria through studio.criterion.*, and every transformation-facing screen (WeightSets, Scorecard, Rankings) names them through prioritization.criterion.* in both languages. The stable key and B0076 are shown beside the label, so each row stays identifiable. There is no data, calculation, pin, authorization, approval or export effect, and no DG5 acceptance clause names this label. It is Low and non-mandatory. The bilingual-string rule is met everywhere a user acts on the weights. This is an admin-only fallback of the same class as the D-079 labelEn limitation, which the DG3 audit carried to DG6 (REQ-S15-007/009). Accepted as an observation for DG5, not closed as fixed. DG6 follow-up (owner frontend-ux-engineer): elementLabel falls back to sourceLabelEn in English, or labelEn is seeded by a new migration (never edit 0062). Prefill 'Label (English)' in the Edit dialog the same way. Add a component test that the English table shows 'Strategic fit' for strategic_fit. Align studio.criterion.time_to_value ('Time to value') with B0076 'Time-to-value'.

Independently judged by release-auditor (T-DG5-RG2-AUDIT-V, session 69bfb4f2) on candidate sha256:55a411ae9f4e87473478988f3d9909752a934a547ba40acc1479f2b2bc3a24ce (source 660f40c7d141b6fb73c145e0ee7a053ceb5905de), in my own complete clone. Both halves are confirmed. (1) In config-resolver.ts:212 the flag is 'overridden: row !== undefined', meaning the version holds its own row. ElementsSection.tsx:403-404 renders that flag as studio.elements.overridden ('Changed' / 'معدّل'), so the column reports 'has an own row', not 'value differs'. In screens/en/dom-p3-published.png all five weights read 'Changed', although only strategic_fit and financial_value changed. (2) displayValue() (studio/api.ts:149-157) JSON-stringifies non-scalar values, so VersionPage.tsx:502/505 prints the rubric levels array as raw JSON. Why this is not blocking: diff.ts compares the RESOLVED elements of both versions, and in the same screenshot the side-by-side 'Differences from the base version' lists exactly strategic_fit 25.00->30.00, financial_value 25.00->20.00 and the feasibility rubric, whose new descriptor is legible. The Compatibility check names the same three elements. A Studio reviewer therefore has an accurate, complete change list, and the misleading column can neither hide nor invent a published change. Review, publish refusal, immutability and pins are unaffected, and REQ-S06-007's acceptance ('the diff lists the added field') is met. It is Low, non-mandatory and presentation only. Accepted as an observation for DG5, not closed as fixed. DG6 follow-up (owner frontend-ux-engineer; backend-workflow-engineer if the API must expose a value-changed flag): show 'Changed' only when the resolved value differs from the base version (or relabel the flag, e.g. 'Set in this version'). Render rubric levels as readable per-score before/after descriptors in en and ar, never raw JSON. Add en and ar tests for both.
